actions.name: Run a FROST key ceremony for an Orchard account
actions.summary: The participants run FROST's distributed key generation over Pallas in the room. Each ends with a share of the spend authorizing key ask; no one holds ask itself. The group key becomes ak. One participant then generates nk and rivk and seals the full viewing key to the others, and each derives the same Orchard address.

fields.name: network
fields.means: the Zcash network (CAIP-2)

fields.name: t
fields.means: how many participants must sign a spend

fields.name: n
fields.means: how many participants hold a share

fields.name: participants
fields.means: the members taking part, named by their room identity keys, which authenticate their packages

fields.name: ciphersuite
fields.means: FROST(Pallas, BLAKE2b-512), the re-randomizable ciphersuite ZIP-312 defines for Orchard

agreement.threshold: all n participants must finish (the DKG aborts on a fault); the key it makes is t of n

requirements.name: room-identity
requirements.target: the member's bound room identity, which authenticates their round-1 and round-2 packages

steps.does: opens the ceremony: network, t, n and the participants.

part 1: each participant's keystore draws a secret polynomial and posts its round-1 package (commitments to the coefficients and a proof of knowledge) to the room log. The room is the broadcast channel the DKG needs: every member reads the same log, so every participant sees the same commitments. The secret part stays in the keystore.
steps.signs: the member's muster attestation over the package; the proof of knowledge is FROST's own

steps.does: part 2: each keystore checks every round-1 package and makes one secret share for each other participant. Each share is sealed to its recipient's encryption key before it enters the log. Only the recipient can open it; other members and the store node see only its size and timing. This replaces frostd, which relays but cannot enforce encryption.
steps.signs: the member's muster attestation over the sealed packages

steps.does: part 3, local: each keystore checks the shares it received against the senders' commitments and keeps its signing share (never in the log). All participants compute the same public key package: the group key and each verifying share. If the group key's ỹ bit is 1, the key and every share are negated, as Orchard key derivation requires.

one participant generates nk and rivk at random and seals the full viewing key (ak, nk, rivk) to every participant. Each participant derives the default Orchard address from it and checks it. The account (address, ak, t, n) is disclosed into the room.

refusals.what: a package from someone outside the participant list, or two different round-1 packages from one participant
refusals.why: the DKG needs authenticated senders and one broadcast view; the FROST book says without a proper broadcast channel key generation is insecure

refusals.what: a round-2 share posted in the clear
refusals.why: anyone who reads the round-2 packages can recreate the secret; they MUST be encrypted

refusals.what: a received share that does not match its sender's round-1 commitments
refusals.why: part 3 fails and the ceremony aborts; the log names who sent it

refusals.what: a group key used with its ỹ bit set to 1
refusals.why: Orchard key derivation negates ask so that ak's ỹ bit is 0; the shares must be negated to match

refusals.what: an address that does not derive from the disclosed ak and the shared nk and rivk
refusals.why: invariant 1: the account is re-derived by every participant, never taken on trust

claims.claim: no one ever holds the whole spend authorizing key
round-2 shares are sealed end to end and every sender is authenticated by the room; no relay server is involved
every participant holds the full viewing key and can see every transaction of the account, for as long as the account exists
claims.party: every participant, and anyone they give the key to

claims.claim: a room member who is not a participant cannot check that the address belongs to ak without the viewing key
claims.party: the participant who discloses the account

claims.claim: the chain learns nothing at setup

evidence.what: ZIP-312 (Draft): FROST for spend authorization; FROST(Pallas, BLAKE2b-512); key generation out of scope but must be consistent with FROST
the ZF FROST DKG: part1 broadcast, part2 private and encrypted, part3 local; the broadcast and encryption requirements
Zcash FROST: DKG yields ask shares and ak; nk and rivk come from an sk or are generated separately
Zcash protocol spec §4.2.3 Orchard key components: ak's ỹ bit is 0 (ask negated otherwise); ivk from ak, nk, rivk
reddsa 0.5.2 FROST(Pallas): the EvenY post-DKG step negates the group key and shares
the ZF demo: DKG with frost-client, then zcash-sign generate --ak to make the address and viewing key
frostd: a relay; messages MUST be end-to-end encrypted, which the server cannot enforce
reddsa 0.6.0 (2026-09-25) removed the frost feature; the FROST ciphersuites will move to the frost repository

unverified: who generates nk and rivk in deployed tools, and whether they can come from a DKG instead of one participant's randomness
where the FROST(Pallas) ciphersuite and its EvenY step live after reddsa 0.6.0 removed them

actions.name: Send a shielded payment (Orchard to Orchard)
actions.summary: Any t participants authorize a fully shielded payment. The proposer builds the transaction; every signer recomputes its ZIP-244 SIGHASH before signing. The chain sees nullifiers, note commitments, randomized keys, the fee and the expiry height. It does not see the amount, the recipient, the group, or who signed.

fields.name: spends
fields.means: each Orchard note spent: value, rho, rseed, its Merkle witness to the anchor, and α, the spend authorization randomizer the proposer chose for its action

fields.name: outputs
fields.means: each recipient's Orchard receiver (from a Unified Address), value and memo, with the note randomness

fields.name: anchor
fields.means: the Orchard note commitment tree root the witnesses prove membership in

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the ZIP-317 fee; with no transparent parts it equals valueBalanceOrchard

fields.name: expiry_height
fields.means: nExpiryHeight: the last height at which the transaction can be mined

fields.name: consensus_branch_id
fields.means: the network upgrade the SIGHASH commits to

fields.name: openings
fields.means: the value commitment trapdoors and output encryption randomness, so every signer can recompute the action descriptions and the SIGHASH

requirements.name: lightwalletd
requirements.target: a lightwalletd or Zaino server the user configures: compact blocks, tree state, broadcast

requirements.name: orchard-full-viewing-key
requirements.target: the account's full viewing key; the prover needs it

requirements.name: orchard-frost-share
requirements.target: a signing share from the account's ceremony

requirements.name: ZEC
requirements.target: Orchard notes the account's viewing key decrypts

steps.does: as the Constructor: syncs through the user's lightwalletd, reads the anchor and each note's witness (external reads, invariant 10), picks notes, chooses a fresh α for each spend action, sets the expiry height (40 blocks ahead by default) and the ZIP-317 fee, and writes the effect. Every member's client recomputes each action and the SIGHASH from the openings, and checks each action's rk = ak + [α]G.
round 1: each signer's keystore draws a hiding and a binding nonce for each spend action and keeps them; the member posts the commitments. Any t participants may take part.
steps.signs: nothing yet. The contribution carries the member's muster attestation over P.

steps.does: round 2: once t commitments are in the log for an action, every member forms the same signing package in the log's canonical order. With that action's α as the randomizer, the keystore signs and erases the nonces.
steps.signs: the ZIP-244 signature digest for SIGHASH_ALL, not tied to any input: BLAKE2b-256 over the header (version, version group, consensus_branch_id, lock_time, expiry_height), the transparent and Sapling digests, and the Orchard digest (each action's nullifier, cmx, ephemeral key, ciphertexts, cv_net and rk; flags; valueBalanceOrchard; anchor). One re-randomized FROST(Pallas, BLAKE2b-512) signature share per spend action, under rsk = ask + α. Plus the member's muster attestation over P.

steps.does: a participant (the prover needs the full viewing key) combines the shares into one RedPallas spendAuthSig per action and checks each under its rk. It makes the Halo 2 proof and the binding signature from the value commitment trapdoors, then broadcasts through the user's lightwalletd.
watches until the transaction is mined. If the expiry height passes first, the transaction is invalid everywhere, and the payment starts again with a new SIGHASH and fresh nonces.

refusals.what: a SIGHASH that is not the one recomputed from the transaction data
refusals.why: invariant 1; ZIP-312: signers MUST check the SIGHASH against the data or compute it themselves

refusals.what: an action whose rk is not ak + [α]G
refusals.why: the signature would authorize a key that is not the group's; α is also what the signers randomize with

refusals.what: a note the account's viewing key does not decrypt (a foreign note)
refusals.why: the room spends from this account only; the proof would fail for another key anyway

refusals.what: a transparent input
refusals.why: transparent inputs use ECDSA; FROST cannot sign them

refusals.what: an expiry height of 0 (never expires) or one at or below the current height
refusals.why: invariant 2 needs an expiry; an expired transaction is invalid in any block (ZIP-203)

refusals.what: a consensus_branch_id that is not the network's current upgrade
refusals.why: the SIGHASH commits to it, so the transaction would be invalid

refusals.what: a fee below the ZIP-317 conventional fee
refusals.why: nodes may drop transactions with unpaid actions

refusals.what: a second signature with the same nonces, or nonces restored after a restart
refusals.why: reusing FROST nonces reveals the signer's share; the keystore erases them on use, and a restart aborts the session

claims.claim: every signer recomputes the SIGHASH from the transaction data before signing; a mismatch is refused
the chain sees no amount, no recipient, no group and no signer
a collected signature is useless after the expiry height, which muster never leaves at 0 (no expiry)
every participant sees the payment through the full viewing key
the proposer, as the Constructor, chooses α; signers check rk but cannot check that α was random, and ZIP-312 says a rogue coordinator can break unlinkability
the lightwalletd server sees the signed transaction before it is mined
claims.party: the user-configured lightwalletd or Zaino server

evidence.what: ZIP-312 (Draft): re-randomized FROST for spend authorization; signers MUST check or compute the SIGHASH; a rogue coordinator can break unlinkability
ZIP-244: the v5 transaction digest; the header commits to consensus_branch_id and expiry_height; Orchard signatures use SIGHASH_ALL
Zcash protocol spec §4.15: a fresh α per Action, rk from ask + α, spendAuthSig over SigHash; §4.14 the Orchard binding signature
ZIP-203: nExpiryHeight; default 40 blocks since Blossom; 0 means no expiry; expired transactions are invalid
ZIP-317: conventional fee = 5000 zatoshis × max(2, logical actions)
RFC 9591 FROST: two-round signing, nonces used once
orchard crate PCZT: α is chosen by the Constructor and needed by the Signer; the Prover needs the full viewing key
frost-rerandomized: re-randomized FROST signing; a randomizer sent over a confidential channel, or derived from the commitments and a seed
frost-tools: frostd, frost-client, zcash-sign; demo only, not for production

unverified: how deployed tools order the randomizer and the SIGHASH: ZIP-312 hashes the message into the randomizer, yet the ZIP-244 SIGHASH commits to each action's rk, which the randomizer determines
whether a PCZT can carry FROST round data to signers outside Muster
whether zcash-sign runs one signing session per spend action (the demo describes one randomizer per session)

actions.name: Pay a transparent address from the shielded account
actions.summary: The same t-of-n shielded spend, paying a transparent address. The chain now sees the amount and the recipient. It still does not see which notes paid, the group, or who signed.

fields.name: spends
fields.means: each Orchard note spent, with its witness and the α for its action

fields.name: transparent-outputs
fields.means: each transparent address and value

fields.name: outputs
fields.means: any Orchard change back to the account

fields.name: anchor
fields.means: the Orchard note commitment tree root

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the ZIP-317 fee

fields.name: expiry_height
fields.means: nExpiryHeight

fields.name: consensus_branch_id
fields.means: the network upgrade the SIGHASH commits to

fields.name: openings
fields.means: the randomness every signer needs to recompute the actions and the SIGHASH

requirements.name: lightwalletd
requirements.target: a lightwalletd or Zaino server the user configures

requirements.name: orchard-full-viewing-key
requirements.target: the account's full viewing key; the prover needs it

requirements.name: orchard-frost-share
requirements.target: a signing share from the account's ceremony

requirements.name: ZEC
requirements.target: Orchard notes the account's viewing key decrypts

steps.does: builds the transaction as for a shielded spend, with a transparent output. valueBalanceOrchard is positive: it carries the payment and the fee out of the Orchard pool. Every member's client recomputes the actions and the SIGHASH and checks each rk.
round 1: each signer posts nonce commitments per spend action.
steps.signs: nothing yet. The contribution carries the member's muster attestation over P.

steps.does: round 2: each signer makes one re-randomized share per spend action.
steps.signs: the ZIP-244 SIGHASH_ALL digest, which here also commits to the transparent outputs, as one FROST(Pallas, BLAKE2b-512) share per spend action under rsk = ask + α. Plus the member's muster attestation over P.

steps.does: a participant combines the shares, proves, adds the binding signature and broadcasts.

refusals.what: a SIGHASH that is not the one recomputed from the transaction data
refusals.why: invariant 1; ZIP-312

refusals.what: an action whose rk is not ak + [α]G, a foreign note, or a transparent input
refusals.why: the same checks as a shielded spend

refusals.what: an expiry height of 0 or already passed, a stale consensus_branch_id, or a fee below ZIP-317
refusals.why: the same checks as a shielded spend

claims.claim: the chain learns the amount and the transparent recipient
the chain does not learn which notes paid, the group, or who signed
every signer recomputes the SIGHASH, transparent outputs included, before signing

evidence.what: Zcash protocol spec §4.14: a positive Orchard balancing value moves value to the transparent pool
ZIP-244: the SIGHASH_ALL digest covers the transparent outputs and the Orchard bundle
ZIP-312: re-randomized FROST for spend authorization
FROST works with Sapling and Orchard only; transparent addresses use ECDSA

actions.name: Refresh shares (remove a participant, keep the address)
actions.summary: The continuing participants re-deal their shares with FROST's refresh DKG. The group key, the viewing key and the address stay the same. Anyone left out is removed as a signer. The threshold cannot change, and no one can be added this way: adding a member means a new ceremony and a new address.

fields.name: participants
fields.means: the continuing participants, at least t

fields.name: removed
fields.means: the participants left out

fields.name: t
fields.means: the threshold, unchanged

agreement.threshold: every continuing participant must finish; the key stays t of the new n

steps.does: names the continuing participants (at least t) and who is removed.
part 1: each continuing participant runs the refresh DKG's first part and posts its package to the log.
steps.signs: the member's muster attestation over the package

steps.does: part 2: each makes one refreshing share per other continuing participant, sealed to its recipient.
steps.signs: the member's muster attestation over the sealed packages

steps.does: part 3, local: each keystore computes its refreshed share. The group key is unchanged; the verifying shares change. Each participant deletes its old share only after every continuing participant reports success.

refusals.what: a refresh that changes the threshold
refusals.why: the refresh procedure cannot change or reduce the threshold

refusals.what: fewer than t continuing participants
refusals.why: the refresh needs at least t participants

refusals.what: adding a participant through a refresh
refusals.why: refresh takes a subset of the current identifiers; a new member needs a new ceremony and a new address

refusals.what: deleting old shares before every continuing participant has refreshed
refusals.why: the FROST book says to confirm everyone succeeded before deleting old key packages

claims.claim: the chain learns nothing: the address and the key do not change
a removed participant can sign again only together with t−1 old shares, so removal holds only if the continuing participants delete theirs
a removed participant keeps the full viewing key and still sees every transaction of the account

evidence.what: frost-core refresh: participants left out are removed; the threshold cannot change; the group key stays the same, the verifying shares change
the FROST book: delete old key packages only after every participant has refreshed
Zcash protocol spec §4.2.3: the full viewing key (ak, nk, rivk) does not depend on the shares

unverified: whether the refresh DKG keeps the Orchard even-Y normalization for FROST(Pallas)
